reasoning: Flight Centre shares fell after a soft Q1 trading update reflecting airfare price deflation and some corporate account downtrading. quote: Flight Centre (Long -25%) shares fell after the company provided a softer Q1 trading update noting impacts from airfare price deflation and downtrading in some corporate accounts. While there may be near-term volatility driven by moderating travel activity, we believe the business is much more efficient and productive than it was relative to its pre-COVID position. On the Leisure side, more than half of the legacy retail store network has been closed and the remaining footprint optimised to generate better returns. The company has also shifted the mix towards more luxury travel and independent store networks. On the corporate side, the business continues to grow strongly and is now the third largest corporate travel manager globally. The company continues to focus on generating a 2% underlying profit before tax (PBT) margin over the medium-term, which, if achieved, would imply a greater than 50% increase in PBT from 2024 levels. Trading on only ~13x FY25 consensus earnings, with a strong balance sheet position, we believe Flight Centre remains an attractive opportunity and have used the sell-off to add to our position.

headline: Greencape reduced its Flight Centre position into share price strength, citing uncertainty around recovery timing and reduced margin of safety, while retaining a holding
reasoning: Flight Centre suffered severe working capital stress as forward bookings collapsed under COVID-19, requiring a heavily dilutionary capital raise in April in which Greencape participated. The firm sees a sustainable long-term role for FLT in leisure travel distribution (particularly complex, high-value bookings) and corporate travel, where it has a $9bn TTV business. Leisure channel consolidation — with STA Travel and others closing permanently — should make suppliers more dependent on Flight Centre for distribution. However, corporate travel is expected to remain structurally smaller for years due to videoconferencing, duty-of-care concerns and budget constraints, with growth dependent on customer acquisition. Greencape trimmed the position into rally-driven strength reflecting inherent recovery uncertainty and a reduced margin of safety.
quote: Whilst the stock remains in the portfolio, we have reduced the position into strength to reflect the inherent uncertainty of the recovery and reduced margin of safety given the rally of the share price. Flight Centre also has a scale Corporate Travel business which generated $9bn of group TTV, or around 38% of the group in FY19. The company has publicly acknowledged that the global Corporate travel market will be smaller for many years, given new ways of working (e.g. Zoom), company duty of care for employees, budget constraints and expected high travel insurance costs for offshore travel. Therefore, the predominant avenue of growth for the Corporate business over the medium term will be via customer acquisition, of which the company has managed to execute on successfully since the onset of the pandemic. At a group level, the company has undertaken significant restructuring and taken considerable costs out of the business which should translate to strong operating leverage into any recovery.
episode_title: GBF FR FullReport 202009
